rationale: ROUND 2 (RESUBMIT_CORR=f3716ebe-e420-4ae9-ba4a-9a649e3d7124). Round 1 returned REVISE on a gating HIGH from bug_historian: bugs_open/085 ('render data advertises current_page and always supplies empty') was still in bugs_open/ and the plan never mentioned it. ANSWERED AT THE FILE AND THE CODE: 085 is NOT open — its own '2026-07-27 (evening)' section records BOTH PATHS VERIFIED LIVE across the v1.0.1173→v1.0.1174 roll (3 charts → 1 chart, same agent/page/reason, only the binary differed); the header's 'inert until the next roll' was written that morning and never updated, so the file's LOCATION lied about its status for three weeks. Reconciled and MOVED to bugs_closed/ (commit 916c8b22b, both paths on the commit; header struck through with a dated correction; a dated closing section written) under the owner's 2026-08-12 bar. Its RELATION to this plan, written into that section: 085 is about the VALUE (the page's name reached the template empty — three drop points on one journey + a fourth on the rerender path; its fix PRODUCES the value via resolveCurrentPageName at build and base[...] at rerender, serialises, restores, projects); step 4 is about the KEY (that string filed under `current_page`, the same key the page RECORD holds at input_data.current_page). Independent in both directions: (i) 085's own end-to-end test TestCurrentPageSurvivesBothRenderPaths is RETAINED and passes under the rename, and FAILS under mutant M4 (drop the step-name read) — it is one of the six mutants this change was proved against, so the value path 085 fixed is demonstrably intact; (ii) a recurrence of 085's emptiness would now emit current_page_name:"" — no key collision either way — so it CANNOT confound the step-4 done-condition, which counts key collisions not values (an empty value is caught by 085's test and a rendered page, never by the conflict count); (iii) [INFERRED, not measurable — the instrument exists only since 08-15] before 085's fix, current_page:"" vs the record would also have been DeepEqual-unequal, so the collision PREDATES 085's fix. GUARDIAN (medium, edit 4 — the renderEnvelopeIdentity landmine): quoted and engaged. The landmine 'The save seam's identity paths resolve to NOTHING inside the page writer's own run' says DO NOT copy save_page_sections' paths (site_record.site_id 0/110, current_page.name 0/110) and that WHAT WORKS is the measured chain input_data.current_page.name → input_data.page_name → render_context.current_page (a plain STRING). This edit does not copy the save seam's paths; it follows the landmine's own measured chain and adds the NEW spelling of its third rung — because that rung is the very key this change renames, the chain HAD to gain it or a post-roll tree would lose its third rung. Re-measured 2026-08-19 on all 49 stored pcw runs (orchestration_states, owner_agent_type='page-content-writer'): rung 1 input_data.current_page.name 49/49, rung 2 input_data.page_name 0/49, rung 3 render_context.current_page is a STRING 49/49, only-rung-3-resolves 0/49 — so today rung 1 covers everything and the new path is belt-and-braces; the old path stays for pre-roll trees. The landmine entry itself now carries a dated correction naming render_context.current_page_name (commit cc1db051a) and the verifier was dispatched (corr ad93974c). EDITQUALITY's soft gap ('same map under output_field AND step name' was inherited, not verified): VERIFIED at code AND data — platform/orchestration/coordinator.go:1902-1906 storeActionResult writes state.CollectedData[state.CurrentStep] = result and then state.CollectedData[step.OutputField] = result (the SAME map), and 49/49 stored pcw runs carry both keys with identical values. EDITQUALITY low + BUG_HISTORIAN low (tolerance has no expiry; a RECORD under the old key is silently ignored): both now written INTO the code comment on setRenderContextScalarsFromData (commit 916c8b22b): the fallback is string-only BY DESIGN (the record has no name to take here), and it is time-bounded with a named retirement — delete it in the §10.13 STEP-5 commit, which by its gate lands after this roll; orchestration_states retention is ~24 h measured (49 pcw rows span 2026-08-18 20:46Z → 2026-08-19 20:06Z), so by then no pre-roll tree can exist; the handoff checklist carries the same item so it cannot outlive its reason quietly. The 051/052 precedent the historian cited is acknowledged in that comment as exactly the failure being avoided. BUG_HISTORIAN medium (the generic mechanism will reproduce for the next pair): agreed and now NAMED in the rename-map comment and in RFC_029 §10.14 / the lane RUNBOOK — the candidate-set query is how the next pair is recognised, a second map entry needs its producer read first, and step 5 is what makes the next collision LOUD instead of a row. PRIOR_ART_LIBRARIAN medium (census figures not checkable) — the exact queries are now in grounded_in, verbatim, so a reviewer can re-run them; low (precedent shape exists?) — renderContextUnserialised is v3_site_actions.go:1692 and renderContextControlFields :1717, both maps of key→reason, both consulted by renderContextStepContractExcluded :1727; REUSE_AGENT (an existing generic step-boundary alias mechanism?) — grep'd: the only alias mechanisms in platform/orchestration are (a) input_contracts/input_mapping.go — declarative, config-level, per call_agent step; (b) the resolver's read-side field-alias arm in datahelpers.extractSingleField (searches ALTERNATIVE names for a requested field — the opposite direction; using it would make the resolver ALSO find current_page_name, which is precisely what must not happen). Neither operates at the Go struct→step-output projection; there was nothing to extend. GUARDIAN low (atomic commit): done — the change landed as ONE pathspec commit of 9 files (1a82225ec); `git diff --numstat` on every file was read before committing; HEAD was built and tested from `git archive` afterwards (ok/ok). No behaviour changed in round 2: the only code delta is comments (916c8b22b); the tests, mutants and the resolver-seam control stand as in round 1. ORIGINAL ROUND-1 RATIONALE FOLLOWS. RFC_029 §10.13 STEP 4 (owner-ruled sequence A, 2026-08-18): fix the surviving resolver shape-conflict AT SOURCE. After the v1.0.1315 roll the conflict population is ONE candidate set (measured 2026-08-19 12:16→16:08Z: 23 rows, 100% of the class): page-content-writer's generate_content step requests `current_page` (its prompt reads {{.current_page.title}} — it needs the page RECORD), and the resolver's whole-tree search collects the record at input_data.current_page / ~unwrap.current_page AND the page NAME STRING that build_render_context files under render_context.current_page and build_render_context.current_page (same step output, filed under output_field and step name). Two TYPES share one key in one collected_data tree; reflect.DeepEqual says they differ; a RESOLVER_CONFLICTING_CANDIDATES row is written on EVERY run. The winner is always the record (bugs_open/306's declared tie-break pins it), so no page was ever wrong — but this is a permanent false-positive population that blocks step 5 (conflicts → refusal) for ever: refusing would strip the page record from generate_content in 100% of runs. THE FIX: one name for the object, another for the string, at the boundary where they met. RenderContext's json tag is the SINGLE declaration of a field's template key (bugs_open/109) and therefore also its step-boundary key; this change introduces a small, reasoned rename map — renderContextStepContractRenames = {"current_page": "current_page_name"} — applied symmetrically at the two ends of the step contract: renderCtxToMap EMITS the page name as current_page_name (and refuses to re-emit the old key from the ContentData merge that follows), setRenderContextScalarsFromData READS current_page_name first and tolerates a STRING under the old spelling for trees written before the roll (read side only). The TEMPLATE contract is deliberately NOT renamed: components still read {{.current_page}} (the struct field is projected under its tag on the render side), because there the key is unambiguous, it is advertised to component authors, and renaming it would have to be coordinated with a live template edit across a roll. The rerender path's hand-built base map (buildRerenderBaseData, the restore contract's second producer) moves to the step name via the same helper; render_content_envelope_guard's identity chain gains render_context.current_page_name AHEAD of the old path, which stays for pre-roll trees. CONSUMERS ENUMERATED (2026-07-29 §3 — named and told, not merely measured): readers of the STEP-BOUNDARY key — Go: renderEnvelopeIdentity (updated here), mergeIntoRenderContext's four call sites (all go through the symmetric restore), buildRerenderBaseData (updated here); config: 0 of the live agent_definitions mention render_context.current_page or build_render_context.current_page; readers of the TEMPLATE key (unaffected): 1 of 306 content_components across every component_level (evidence-chart, `$page := .current_page`), 0 of 265 component_versions, 0 Go-embedded templates, 0 agent prompts advertising {{.current_page}} as a bare variable; structuralFields in v3_site_actions.go still lists current_page, correctly. PROOF: 7 tests pin both halves and were mutation-proved SIX ways (emit under the template key; drop the ContentData skip; drop the legacy read fallback; drop the step-name read; base map under the old key; envelope chain without the new path — each fails a NAMED test; package compiles throughout). Plus a test at the resolver seam itself: the real datahelpers.ExtractFields over a live-shaped tree with renderCtxToMap's real output records ZERO conflicts and returns the record, and a CONTROL with the pre-rename shape still records one (the instrument is proven live in the test, so the zero is not a silent instrument). REJECTED ALTERNATIVES: (a) rename the json tag itself — renames the template contract as a side effect (structuralFields, evidence-chart, every future author), needs a live template edit ordered against the roll, and widens scope into a namespace with no defect; (b) a type-aware search (accept only map-shaped current_page) — bakes schema knowledge into a shared resolver, wider blast radius than renaming one key at one producer; (c) a `!` strict marker — impossible, generate_content's request list is Go-side. Behaviour change is confined to the step output key; every template sees exactly what it saw. Inert until the next chassis roll; the done-condition is RFC_029 §10.13 step 4's: the pcw `current_page` conflict class reads ZERO in the post-roll window against live demand (pcw runs present), after which step 5 is buildable.

plan.risks: (1) Trees in flight across the roll hold render_context.current_page (string) written by the old binary and are restored by the new one — covered by the read-side tolerance (TestRestoreAcceptsBothSpellingsAcrossTheRoll 'old tree' case) and the envelope chain keeping the old path; the html/template path would also survive on the ContentData catch-all alone. (2) A NEW string candidate could appear if some other step files a `current_page` string into collected_data — the resolver-seam test and the post-roll window read (same query as grounded_in[0]) are the detectors; today's population is exactly one set and this change ends it. (3) The tolerance keeps `current_page` as an ACCEPTED restore key, which a reader could mistake for a sanctioned emit name — the comment on setRenderContextScalarsFromData says read-side-only, and TestStepOutputNeverCarriesCurrentPage makes an emit under the old name a failing test. (4) Templates now ALSO receive `.current_page_name` via the ContentData catch-all on restore (every step-output key does, e.g. _sources_merged) — harmless extra key; `.current_page` is unchanged. (5) NOT a config change and NOT a template change: nothing to order against the roll; inert until the next chassis build. Verification after the roll: stamp the binary (known-absent + known-present controls), then the grounded_in[0] query over the post-roll window must read 0 rows for pcw/current_page against live pcw demand (orchestrations referencing page-content-writer in the window); a zero with no pcw runs is not evidence. ROUND 2 additions: (6) bugs 085 is CLOSED and independent (value vs key) — its retained test is mutation-checked against this change; an 085-shape regression emits current_page_name:"" and cannot register as a conflict row, so it cannot confound the step-4 done-condition. (7) The read-side tolerance now has a named owner for its removal (the step-5 commit) and the handoff carries it; if step 5 is delayed past a week the tolerance is still harmless (string-only, read-only) but should be removed on its own.
